assessment: The manager will assess the performance of the employee over the appraisal period against each of the criteria in the capability framework. There are 4 possible levels of assessment for each criterion.
The employee exceeds the standard for this criterion—they are performing at a higher level of classification
The employee meets the standard to a high degree, but does not meet the standard required for the next highest level of classification
The employee meets the standard for this criterion at their current classification level—they are performing fully
The employee is developing their capability at this level of classification
There are four possible overall assessments:

The employee has performed consistently at a higher standard than expected for their classification. This requires 5 criteria scored at a level of 1 and no criteria scored at a level of 3. Consideration should be given to these staff receiving a promotion or a performance bonus.

The employee has performed at or above the standard expected for their classification level for all criteria. This requires a score of 2 or higher for all criteria. High performing staff would be expected to receive this rating.
The employee is meeting performance expectations. This requires a rating of 2 or higher in at least 5 criteria. Most staff would be expected to receive this rating.

The employee is still developing to standard for their current classification level. This will result from a rating of 3 in four or more criteria. Most newly promoted staff would be expected to receive this rating.
